correctness.rationale: Fresh enumeration checked the defining separation condition on all 296010 six-subsets of the 27 possible columns and all 888030 seven-subsets. Exactly 36 six-subsets are valid and no seven-subset is valid, so heredity gives the sharp maximum six. Applying all 1296 standard row/symbol transformations to the 36 maxima gives one orbit of size 36, hence stabilizer 36. This independently reconstructs the package's certificate without relying on its stored classification file.

No inspected source proves that seven columns are impossible, counts the 36 labeled six-column families, or proves they are one equivalence orbit. Those are the audited contributions.

value.rationale: The three-row ternary case is the smallest genuinely nontrivial perfect-hash parameter where a six-column construction has long been known but an exact all-family census is not supplied by the standard tables. Closing the upper bound and proving one-orbit rigidity is a natural finite classification with clear reference value.

final_claim: A three-row ternary perfect hash family of strength three has at most six columns; exactly 36 labeled six-column maxima exist, and under row permutations and independent symbol permutations in the three rows all 36 form a single equivalence class with stabilizer size 36.
limitations: The six-column construction itself is prior art.
The classification is only for three rows, alphabet three, strength three.
